title: Landing Gear Bay Wiring — Bay Roof Route, Terminal Block and Door Position Circuits

ata.title: Centre Fuselage Wiring — Landing Gear Bay Wiring

abstract: Wiring diagram sheet for the main landing gear bay, showing the bay roof route, the terminal block and bus bar positions and the door position circuits, with the actuator clearance value.

sections.purpose: This sheet shows the main landing gear bay wiring, the bay roof route, the terminal block and bus bar positions and the gear door position circuits, for all ZEPHYR-22 family aircraft.
sections.sheet_note: The sheet is drawn for the left bay; the right bay is a mirror image with the same harness references and a terminal block on the opposite side wall. The clearance value between the harness and the gear door actuator is stated on the sheet for three door positions and it is the design value, not a workmanship tolerance; it is the reason this route must be surveyed whenever a component in the bay is changed.
sections.routing_note: The harness enters the bay at the centre fuselage penetration and runs aft along the bay roof through zones 145 and 721 to the terminal block on the side wall, then outboard to the door position sensors in zone 572. Cable ties must be of the section given on the sheet; an over-tightened tie of the wrong section cuts the harness sleeve without any visible damage to the outer jacket. Any support disturbed during a component change must be re-established at the original station.

ata.title: Centre Fuselage Wiring — Landing Gear Bay Wiring

abstract: Wiring diagram sheet for the main landing gear bay covering both roof routes, the terminal block and bus bar positions and the door position circuits, with the three position method that makes the actuator clearance value meaningful.

sections.purpose: This sheet shows the main landing gear bay wiring, the bay roof route, the terminal block and bus bar positions and the gear door position circuits, for all ZEPHYR-22 family aircraft.
sections.sheet_note: The sheet is drawn for the left bay; the right bay is a mirror image with the same harness references and a terminal block on the opposite side wall. The clearance value between the harness and the gear door actuator is stated on the sheet for three door positions and it is the design value, not a workmanship tolerance; it is the reason this route must be surveyed whenever a component in the bay is changed. The three positions are not alternatives. The actuator sweeps through its closest approach near the mid position, so a clearance taken only with the door fully open always passes and tells nobody anything; a survey recorded from one position is not a survey and the sheet value may not be signed against it. The route was moved forty millimetres outboard on later aircraft and both routes are shown, on sheets 1 and 2 respectively, each with its own set of three values.
sections.routing_note: The harness enters the bay at the centre fuselage penetration and runs aft along the bay roof through zones 145 and 721 to the terminal block on the side wall, then outboard to the door position sensors in zone 572. Cable ties must be of the section given on the sheet; an over-tightened tie of the wrong section cuts the harness sleeve without any visible damage to the outer jacket. Any support disturbed during a component change must be re-established at the original station.
